# shiv

An AI assistant that runs in your terminal, on the device.

Talk to a model, let it run commands, keep the conversation across sessions. Bring your own API key — the provider is up to you.

Since **2.0** it can also build tweaks, end to end, without leaving the phone.

## Providers

Moonshot · DeepSeek · OpenAI · OpenRouter · Ollama (local) · custom endpoint

Anything speaking the OpenAI `/chat/completions` format works. Claude is reachable through OpenRouter — Anthropic's own API uses a different shape and isn't supported directly.

## What it does

**Reads and edits files, runs shell commands** — with a permission prompt before anything that could change your device. Reading and listing don't ask.

**Sessions** are saved every turn. Continue with `/continue`, browse older ones with `/resume`, or rewind to an earlier point.

**Background tasks** — `Ctrl+B` sends a running job to the background. Press `↓` to reach the counter, `Enter` for detail, `k` to stop. Output streams while the job is still running.

**Profiles** keep several providers side by side. `/profile` picks who you connect to, `/model` picks what runs.

## Commands

Turkish and English names both work, and a prefix is enough — `/prof`.

`/profile` `/model` `/settings` `/resume` `/continue` `/lang` `/name` `/color` `/new` `/show` `/geo` `/device` `/env` `/mac` `/performance` `/help` `/quit`

### The bug that doesn't announce itself

Write a class name that doesn't exist and the code **compiles**. The tweak **installs**. It **loads**. And then nothing happens — no error, no log, no crash. You stare at working-looking code for hours.

This is the single most common way tweak work goes wrong, and it is why an AI writing tweak code is dangerous unless it can check its work.

### So shiv reads your device

Every jailbroken iPhone already carries the shared cache — every system class, every method, sitting there in `/System/Cryptexes`. shiv parses it directly. No IPSW download, no Mac, no setup.

```
shiv-sinif LockScreen
shiv-sinif --metod SBLockScreenManager
shiv-sinif --metodara notificationCount
```

2190 classes scan in 28 ms. The model runs this itself before writing code, and if it can't confirm a name it says so instead of guessing.

### App Store apps are encrypted

Their class names can't be read from disk — FairPlay encrypts the binary. shiv decrypts on the device, no Mac and no Python needed:

```
shiv-cek <bundle-id>
shiv-oku <bundle-id> [pattern]
```

Measured: YouTube, 196 MB, 32,929 classes recovered. `shiv-oku` reads the class list from a running app instead, which needs no decryption at all.

**These need frida-server, and the version matters.** shiv links frida-core 16, so the server has to be a 16.x build — a 17.x server will not talk to it. On rootless, `shiv-frida-kur` fetches a matching 16.1.4 and pins it. `/env` measures what you have and says so.

### Building for arm64e system processes

Tweaks for App Store apps and command-line tools build on the phone with nothing to think about — those are arm64, there is no pointer authentication.

System processes are arm64e, and there the on-device compiler emits an older pointer-auth ABI. Two things in your code can then trip it: an `@"..."` string literal, and handing a **block** to the system. Hooks, selector calls and ivar reads are fine.

**`oldabi` bridges both.** If it is installed — and it usually is — those tweaks build and run on the phone. `/env` measures whether you have it.

For a package you hand to other people, declare it:

```
Depends: firmware (<< 15.0) | cy+cpu.arm64v8 | oldabi
```

Or build on a Mac with `/mac` for a deb that depends on nothing. shiv explains both and doesn't push one on you.

### Start here

```
/env
```

Measures the whole development environment — jailbreak type, Theos path and flavour, SDKs, frida and its version, `oldabi`, and the build flow it recommends for **your** setup. It **runs** each tool rather than checking that the file exists, so a broken tool shows as broken.

**Node.js is bundled.** Install shiv and it runs — nothing else to add.

**Don't run it as root.** Files would end up owned by root and `~/.shiv` could no longer be written by mobile.

**Your data stays.** Profiles, API keys, sessions and input history live in `~/.shiv`. Removing the package leaves them alone — even on purge.

**Your API key is yours.** Stored locally, sent only to the provider you chose. `/aktar` exports a session with keys and device identifiers stripped.

**`BILGI.md`** — anything you put in `~/.shiv/BILGI.md` is given to the model every session. Write down the quirks of your device once instead of explaining them every time.

Measured on two devices: iPhone 15 Pro (iOS 17.0.3, RootHide) and iPhone XS (iOS 16.1.1, Dopamine rootless). Rootless support was rebuilt in 2.1.0 after measuring on real hardware rather than assuming.

**Known limits.** `.appex` extensions run in their own process and aren't decrypted by this route. Class lookup was verified on iOS 16 and 17 — on another version shiv says it can't confirm rather than returning a wrong name. Rootful jailbreaks rest on documentation, not testing.

The faults that the two-device field test turned up, closed.

**`shiv-sinif` works again.** `dsc-disk.js` was never copied into the package, so a clean install always died with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. Added, and the packaging now verifies it.

**`/env` runs the tools instead of looking for the files.** It used to report `ok` for three tools that were all broken. A tool that fails now shows as failed.

**`shivfrida` disappeared on every reinstall.** The cause was `postrm` with no guard: on a dpkg upgrade it deleted the directory that had just been unpacked. Cleanup is now bound to `remove|purge`, as Debian expects.

**frida version.** shiv links frida-core 16, so the server has to be 16.x — the repo's latest is 17.x and will not talk to it. On rootless, the new `shiv-frida-kur` fetches a matching 16.1.4 and pins it. `/env` measures the version and warns on a mismatch.

**`shiv-cek` on rootless** returned empty fields because the Dopamine bootstrap has no `awk`; rewritten with `tr` and `cut`. It also finds `shivfrida` from its own location now instead of a hard-coded path.

**Mac cross-build** — with `SHIV_NODE_CAPRAZ=1` the bundled iOS node is verified as a Mach-O rather than executed, so debs can be produced on a Mac without a device.

A measurement release, not a feature one. shiv was run on a second device — iPhone XS, iOS 16.1.1, Dopamine rootless — and what 2.0.0 claimed about rootless turned out to be wrong in four places.

### Rootless support, rebuilt

**Environment detection was wrong.** The check was "is `/var/jb` a symlink" — but it is a symlink on Dopamine too, just pointing somewhere else. A rootless device reported itself as RootHide, and every piece of guidance that followed was built on that. Now measured through `/rootfs`, `.jbroot-*` and `readlink /var/jb`.

**`awk` doesn't exist** in the Dopamine bootstrap. `/env` was silently saying "no frida" while frida was running. Rewritten with `sed` and `grep`.

**The home directory was a shadow.** `$HOME` points at `/var/jb/var/mobile` on rootless, so `/aktar` wrote somewhere Files and Filza never show. Now the real `/var/mobile`.

**Frida isn't in the default rootless repos.** `/env` now tells you to add `https://build.frida.re/`.

### Guidance follows the environment

Theos flavour, patcher and the recommended build flow are now chosen from what was measured. A rootless device is no longer told to use the RootHide fork.

`/env` also measures **`oldabi`** now. This mattered more than it looked: on-device `caps 0x00` tweaks were "working" — but that proved `oldabi` was installed, not that the tweak was fine. The model used to say "a tweak with a block needs a Mac build"; that text predated the measurement and has been corrected.

### The packaging debt is closed

`shiv-cek`, `shiv-oku` and `shivfrida` were described in the docs and the changelog but `paketle.sh` only ever copied `shiv-sinif` and `shiv-ortam` — tools that were written about and never shipped. All three are in the deb now (shivfrida 14 MB, arm64e), and packaging ends by extracting them back out of the deb to verify. Missing one stops the build.

### Interface

- Assistant narration is no longer folded; only tool output is (`SHIV_ANLATIM_KATLA=1` restores the old behaviour)
- `Ctrl+G` send-now works again; queued messages show under the spinner
- The language step previews its description in the language under the cursor
- `/env` output reads more cleanly — separate blocks, neutral tone

shiv can now build tweaks end to end, on the device.

### Tweak development

**Class and method lookup** — reads the device's own shared cache, and now also binaries that live outside it (Control Centre modules, Settings bundles, SDKs embedded in apps).

**On-device decryption** — `shiv-cek <bundle-id>` unwraps FairPlay without a Mac or Python. `shiv-oku` lists classes from a running app.

**`/env`** — measures the development environment before work starts: jailbreak type, Theos path and flavour, SDKs, frida, and the build flow it recommends.

**Build guidance** — the model knows which tweaks can be built on the phone and which need a Mac, and explains the difference instead of refusing flatly.

**`TWEAK.md`** ships with the package: measured recipes the model reads when it needs them, so the base prompt stays small.

### Background tasks

`Ctrl+B` sends a running job to the background. `↓` reaches the counter, `Enter` opens detail, `k` stops it. Output streams while the job is still running, and the timer ticks every second.

### Fixed

- **Lines were losing their last character.** The gutter mark `⎿` draws two columns in this terminal while shiv counted one, so every gutter line shifted a column and later redraws clipped the end. Now `└`.
- Command tails (`exit=1`, elapsed time) overflowed the width budget
- `Ctrl+B` was bound twice; the background branch was unreachable
- Fold state is saved, so `/resume` no longer reopens collapsed text
- Sessions broken by a half-finished tool call are repaired on load
- Mac connection and respring now go through the permission prompt

### Documentation

A standalone tweak development guide ships in `belgeler/` — readable on its own, without shiv.

### New

**Class and method lookup** — shiv reads your device's own system libraries, so tweak code uses real names instead of guesses.

**Remote build** — connect a Mac with `/mac` and build there without leaving the app.

**`/device`** — disk, conflicting tweaks, crash history, broken packages.

**`/aktar`** — export a session to a file, API keys stripped.

**`BILGI.md`** — your own notes, given to the model every session.

**Context trimming** — long conversations no longer hit the wall.

### Changed

- Smaller install: 96 → 71 MB
- The model now refuses on-device builds that would trigger Safe Mode, and explains what to do instead

### Fixed

- Setup screen accepted the API key but would not advance
- Working directory could silently reset to the install path
- Crash logs and system paths under `/rootfs` were unreachable
- Long tool sessions could stop without saying why
**Fixed** — entering the API key on the setup screen.

**Node.js is bundled now.** Nothing else to install, on RootHide or rootless.

### New

**Sub-agents — the model can delegate.** Large jobs get split into background sub-tasks that run in parallel: one searches files while another reads logs, and the results come back merged.

**Performance presets** — `/performance`. High, Balanced or Low power. Controls whether markdown is styled while streaming, how often the screen redraws, and how much history stays live.

**Rewind** — take the conversation back to an earlier point. Press `Esc` twice, pick a point, continue from there.

**Background tasks** — `Ctrl+B` sends a running job to the background and tells you when it finishes.

**Startup hints** — short tips appear on the right when you open the app, then fade on their own.

### Changed

**Speed.** Typing, streaming and scrolling were rebuilt. Long sessions no longer slow down; the keyboard stays instant even after hundreds of messages.

**Response time.** The app was sending more than it needed to on every message. Replies start sooner now.

**Look.** New logo, consistent across the app, the icon and this page.

### Fixed

- Wrapped lines keep their indentation
- Code blocks stay inside their border when wrapped
- Arrow keys and `Esc` no longer drop keystrokes
- Held backspace no longer jumps the cursor
- Arrow keys no longer get stuck on commands in history
- A crash on launch
- Streaming slowing down on long replies

**New** — `/context` and `/about`, plus a detailed activity view on `Ctrl+O`.

**Changed** — `/model`, `/profile` and `/lang` are pickable lists now instead of typed arguments. `/settings` reorganised. Panels behave consistently with each other. Clearer message when you interrupt a reply.

**Fixed** — duplicate welcome card; model selection getting lost; Turkish strings showing up in the English interface; words breaking mid-word at the edge; session picker breaking on rotation; command names getting truncated.

**Better** — fewer screen refreshes, and opening or closing the keyboard no longer resizes the panels.

**Rotation is smooth now.** Turning the device reflows the screen to the new width and keeps your conversation with it.

**No more flicker.** Only the parts that actually changed get redrawn, while typing and while a reply streams in.

**Landscape welcome card** — logo on the left, shortcuts and working directory on the right.

**Three new themes.** Switch with `/theme`.

**Command list is navigable.** Walk it with the arrow keys, filter it as you type.

**Working directories** added with `/add-dir` are clearer in the panel.

**Help panel reworked** — two columns in landscape, full description of the selected command in portrait.

- Verified on a rootless device — the rootless build is no longer untested
- Node.js is now in this repo for both RootHide and rootless, so it installs alongside shiv
- Language handling fixed
- `/geo` output reworked

First release.

- Sessions are saved every turn and can be continued or searched
- Several providers side by side, switchable without losing context
- Turkish and English throughout, including the reply language
- Input history with arrow keys and `Ctrl+R` search
- Output panel on `Ctrl+T`
- Multi-line paste arrives as one message instead of one per line
- Two builds: rootless and RootHide
